clue.text: Pub blasted into space? That's not the main story

indicators.note: putting one thing into another means placing it inside

parts.note: a slot is a gap or space to fill

indicators.note: something blasted is blown apart, so its letters land in a new order

parts.note: taken as written, then rearranged

explanation.surface: A pub is launched into outer space, which sounds like a wild side plot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'space' suggests the cosmos after 'blasted', but here it is just a gap to slot something into.
explanation.definitionFit: A subplot is a secondary thread running alongside the principal narrative of a novel or film.

clue.text: Run-down but sounding warm and bright

definitions.note: a noun here: a rundown, a brief account

indicators.note: sounding means we judge the word by how it is spoken, not spelt

parts.note: weather that is warm and bright is like summer

explanation.surface: Someone feels exhausted yet strangely sunny in mood.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Run-down' looks like an adjective meaning tired, but it is the noun rundown, a brief account; SUMMERY and SUMMARY are said alike.
explanation.definitionFit: A rundown is a quick outline of the main points, which is exactly what a summary gives.

clue.text: Support senior team's leads and get on behind the scenes

parts.note: to back someone is to support them

indicators.note: leads are the ones in front, so take the opening letter of each word

parts.note: the first letters of the two words
to get on in years is to age

explanation.surface: Advice to back the senior team's leaders and work your way up quietly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'get on' reads as getting along with people, but here it means growing older.
explanation.definitionFit: Backstage is the area out of the audience's sight in a theatre, so it also means out of public view.

clue.text: Blanket agreement joins basic political adversaries

definitions.note: a noun: a covering spread over something

indicators.note: a link that joins two things sits between them, so one piece goes in the middle

parts.note: Left and Right, the two fundamental political sides, abbreviated
aye is a word of assent, as in a vote

explanation.surface: A sweeping deal brings the main political rivals together.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Blanket agreement' looks like one phrase meaning a general deal; 'Blanket' is the definition, and Left and Right give L and R.
explanation.definitionFit: A blanket of snow or fog is a covering sheet spread over a surface, the same as a stratum.

clue.text: Monarch in total disarray gets a scolding

indicators.note: one thing in another sits inside it
disarray is a state of disorder, so the letters are thrown into a new order

parts.note: taken as written, then rearranged
a king is a monarch

explanation.surface: A king whose affairs are a complete mess receives a dressing-down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'total disarray' reads as one phrase about chaos, but 'total' is the raw material and 'disarray' tells you to mix it.
explanation.definitionFit: Giving someone a talking-to means reprimanding them sharply, an idiom for telling off.

clue.text: Jeweller initially employed on fantastic work unit

indicators.note: in an across clue, one thing on another is placed after it

parts.note: fab is informal for fantastic
the erg is a unit of work in physics

indicators.note: initially points to the very start, so only the opening letter is used

parts.note: the first letter of the word

explanation.surface: A jeweller is first taken on to work in a dazzling workshop.
explanation.walkthrough: The opening letter comes first in the clue but goes last, because 'on' puts it after the rest. The erg is the old CGS unit of work.
explanation.definitionFit: Carl Fabergé was the Russian goldsmith famous for jewelled Easter eggs made for the tsars.

clue.text: Suggest keeping nothing in apartment

indicators.note: to keep something is to hold it, so one piece holds another inside

parts.note: a flat is the British word for an apartment
nothing is zero, which looks like O

explanation.surface: Someone proposes leaving an apartment completely empty.
explanation.walkthrough: FLAT is the British word for an apartment; zero is written as the letter O.
explanation.definitionFit: To float an idea is to put it forward tentatively for others to consider, a figurative sense.

clue.text: Sulphur most volatile in seawater

indicators.note: one thing in another sits inside it

parts.note: brine is salty water such as the sea

indicators.note: volatile means unstable and liable to change, so the letters will not stay put

parts.note: taken as written, then rearranged

explanation.surface: A chemist notes that sulphur is most reactive when dissolved in the sea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'volatile' fits the chemistry surface as a property of sulphur, but it only signals the shuffle.
explanation.definitionFit: Brimstone is the old biblical name for sulphur, as in fire and brimstone.

clue.text: Quote Gorki piece promoting source of alternative meaning?

indicators.note: in a down clue, promoting moves letters upwards, so they read backwards
a piece is a part of something larger, so the letters are a section of the words

parts.note: the letters run across the end of the first word and start of the second

explanation.surface: Someone cites a passage of Maxim Gorky that advances an alternative interpretation.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is cryptic: a thesaurus is where you look up other words with the same meaning, and Roget's is the best known.
explanation.definitionFit: Peter Roget compiled the famous thesaurus, a reference book listing synonyms, words of alternative sense.

clue.text: Blows up as former partner criticises getting custody of daughter

parts.note: an ex is a former partner

indicators.note: having custody of someone means holding them, so one piece is kept inside

parts.note: to pan a show is to criticise it harshly
D is the abbreviation for daughter

explanation.surface: Someone loses their temper because an ex-partner's attacks are winning custody of their daughter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Blows up' suggests losing one's temper, which fits the custody battle, but it means swells.
explanation.definitionFit: Inflating a balloon makes it grow larger, so to blow up is to increase in size.

clue.text: Host reluctant to provide name that's real?

definitions.note: the question mark flags that the name is real only in the phrase 'the real McCoy'

parts.note: an MC, master of ceremonies, hosts an event
coy means unwilling to commit or reveal

explanation.surface: A host is shy about revealing a genuine name.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reluctant to provide name' reads as one idea, but the name is the answer, defined through the phrase 'the real McCoy'.
explanation.definitionFit: The real McCoy is an idiom for the genuine article, so this surname is the one paired with real.

clue.text: Researching optimistic outlook

definitions.meaning: first meaning: consulting a reference to find something

definitions.note: a noun phrase; the answer is the description of such an outlook
definitions.meaning: second meaning: things are improving, as in 'prospects are good'

explanation.walkthrough: The two words read as a phrase about hopeful research; they are separate meanings of one phrasal verb.
explanation.definitionFit: You consult a dictionary to find a word, and when matters improve we say prospects are getting better.

clue.text: Disturbs a lunatic, one saying silly things?

indicators.note: lunatic means crazy, so the letters behave wildly and change order

parts.note: taken as written, then rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone upsets a madman, who then starts talking nonsense.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lunatic' looks like the person being disturbed, but it is the signal to shuffle the two words before it.
explanation.definitionFit: An absurdist writes or speaks in the style of absurdity, producing deliberately nonsensical, ridiculous statements.

clue.text: Determined to attack

definitions.meaning: first meaning: resolved to do something, as in being bent on it
second meaning: to assault, as a dog may be urged against someone

explanation.walkthrough: It reads as one person resolved on an assault; the two parts are separate meanings of the same phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: Being set on a goal means resolute about it, and to be set on by thugs is to be assaulted.

clue.text: Poet's starting yearly excursion around the Shetlands

indicators.note: starting points to the beginning, so take only the opening letter of each word

parts.note: the first letters of the five words

explanation.surface: A poet begins an annual trip round the islands north of Scotland.
explanation.walkthrough: The Shetlands are islands off the far north of Scotland. 'Poet's starting' looks like the poet setting off, but it signals the first letters.
explanation.definitionFit: W B Yeats was the Irish writer of verse who won the Nobel Prize in Literature in 1923.

clue.text: Narrative has tiny roles getting cast

indicators.note: to cast is to throw, and thrown letters land in a different arrangement

parts.note: taken as written, then rearranged

explanation.surface: A play contains small parts, and the actors for them are being chosen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cast' fits the theatre picture as choosing actors for roles, but here it means throwing the letters about.
explanation.definitionFit: A storyline is the plot of a book, play or film, the sequence of events it tells.

clue.text: Elegant but would become loud if Charlie replaced George

indicators.note: to replace is to swap one thing for another, so one letter is exchanged

parts.note: clamorous means noisy
Charlie is C in the NATO phonetic alphabet
George was G in older phonetic alphabets

explanation.surface: Something stylish would turn brash if one man took another's place.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue states it the reverse way: putting C in place of G in the answer makes CLAMOROUS, so the answer has G where loud has C.
explanation.definitionFit: Glamorous describes alluring, stylish beauty, close to the sense of graceful refinement.

clue.text: Two men interrupting occasional audit to make change

indicators.note: to interrupt is to break into, so pieces go inside another
occasional means now and then, so only every other letter is used

parts.note: the first, third and fifth letters
men written twice

explanation.surface: Two people disrupt an irregular inspection of the accounts, hoping to alter it.
explanation.walkthrough: Each MEN goes in a separate gap between the three kept letters, rather than both together.
explanation.definitionFit: An amendment is an alteration, especially a formal one made to a document or law.

clue.text: Very large hint is placed inside bar

parts.note: OS is the clothing size abbreviation for outsize

indicators.note: something placed inside another is held within it

parts.note: a trace is a slight hint of something
taken as written

explanation.surface: A heavy clue is planted in a pub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bar' looks like the place where the hint is hidden, but it is the verb meaning to shut out.
explanation.definitionFit: To ostracise someone is to exclude them from a group, which is what barring does.

clue.text: Put additional backing into call; it's quite an attraction

indicators.note: putting one thing into another means placing it inside

parts.note: to call is to phone

indicators.note: backing means going backwards, so the letters run the other way

parts.note: more means additional

explanation.surface: Someone puts extra support behind a phone call because it draws people in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backing' reads as financial support, but it signals reversal.
explanation.definitionFit: A pheromone is a chemical signal released by animals that draws mates, a literal sexual lure.

clue.text: What to do with guests making fighting challenge?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: give visitors a bed for the night
second meaning: the boxer's invitation to raise your fists

explanation.walkthrough: 'EM is short for them, so the same words mean both offering lodging and inviting a fistfight.
explanation.definitionFit: Hosting visitors overnight is accommodating them, while a pugilist demanding raised fists is daring an opponent to brawl.

clue.text: Consume with worry when facing judge

parts.note: something that worries you is eating you
a defendant is up before the judge

explanation.surface: Someone is eaten up with anxiety while standing trial.
explanation.walkthrough: To be 'up before' a judge or magistrate is to be in court charged with something.
explanation.definitionFit: To eat up food is to finish it completely, so it means devour or use entirely.

clue.text: Talk about defender getting revenge

indicators.note: to turn about is to face the opposite way, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: to yap is to talk noisily
a back is a defensive player in football or rugby

explanation.surface: Gossip about a footballer who is out to settle a score.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' looks like 'concerning', but here it turns the talk round.
explanation.definitionFit: Payback is retaliation, getting even with someone for a wrong they did.

clue.text: Creep sending bill back for present

indicators.note: to send something off is to dispatch it, here in the opposite direction
sending something back returns it the way it came, so the letters face the other way

parts.note: a toady is a sycophant, a creep
an ad is an advertisement, also called a bill or poster

explanation.surface: A sycophant returns an invoice in exchange for a gift.
explanation.walkthrough: Only the two letters inside the creep are turned round, not the whole word. 'present' looks like a gift but means now.
explanation.definitionFit: Today stands for the current era or this very day, the time that is happening now.

clue.text: The same one not drinking during party

indicators.note: something happening during another event falls within it

parts.note: a do is an informal word for a party
the Roman numeral for one
TT stands for teetotal

explanation.surface: The same person stays sober during the party once again.
explanation.walkthrough: TT is short for teetotal, someone who drinks no alcohol; a do is British slang for a party.
explanation.definitionFit: Ditto is used to say that something repeated applies again, meaning likewise or identical.

clue.text: Verbal submission pronounced while seated

definitions.note: an adverbial phrase, while the answer is an adjective

indicators.note: pronounced means spoken, so we go by the sound rather than the spelling

parts.note: an entry that is said rather than written

explanation.surface: A spoken statement is delivered from a chair.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Verbal' looks like the homophone signal, but it belongs to the phrase being sounded; 'pronounced' is the signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Sedentary describes work or habits done sitting down, from Latin for sitting.

clue.text: A prevaricating politician does this on reversing cuts

indicators.note: reversing means going the opposite way, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: snips are small cuts made with scissors

explanation.surface: An evasive politician performs a U-turn on spending cuts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reversing cuts' sounds like a policy U-turn on budget cuts, which fits the slippery politician perfectly.
explanation.definitionFit: Political spin is presenting facts in a slanted way, and evasive politicians routinely put a favourable gloss on news.

clue.text: Mechanic held, for a time, specific job

indicators.note: the words hold the letters only briefly, so they are carried within them

parts.note: the letters span the end of one word and the start of the next

explanation.surface: A mechanic was kept on temporarily for a particular task.
explanation.walkthrough: 'held' looks like the mechanic being kept on in a job, but it is the words holding the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A niche is a role or position that suits someone exactly, a specialised corner of work.

clue.text: Admit rice is rotten — it's fatal for mother

indicators.note: something rotten has gone bad and fallen apart, so its letters recombine

parts.note: taken as written, then rearranged

explanation.surface: A warning that spoiled rice could kill your mum.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Admit' looks like a verb of confession, but it is only part of the letters to be mixed.
explanation.definitionFit: Matricide is the killing of one's own mother, from Latin mater plus the suffix for slaying.

clue.text: Country where its traditional energy source not available

parts.note: chi, or qi, is the life force of traditional Chinese thought
NA is the standard abbreviation for not available

explanation.surface: A nation whose customary power supply has run out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'energy source' suggests coal or oil, but it is the vital energy of Chinese medicine, which 'its' ties to the country.
explanation.definitionFit: China is the populous East Asian nation, the most obvious example of a state.

clue.text: System allowing force to arrest most senior officer

indicators.note: to arrest someone is to seize and hold them, so one piece is held inside

parts.note: to press is to force
OC is the officer commanding a unit

explanation.surface: A procedure lets the police force detain their own top officer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'force' and 'arrest' suggest the police, but force is the verb to press.
explanation.definitionFit: A process is a set series of steps for achieving something, a method or procedure.

clue.text: Blessed group, a subject central to Chekov

parts.note: a theme is a subject or topic

indicators.note: central means at the core, so only the middle letters are used

parts.note: the two middle letters of the six

explanation.surface: A sacred circle has a topic at the heart of its Chekhov reading.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition comes from the Sermon on the Mount: 'Blessed are the meek, for they shall inherit the earth'.
explanation.definitionFit: In the Beatitudes, Jesus names humble, gentle people among those whom God favours.
